name: Gwamhi-Wuri

catalog_quote: Dialects: GWAMHI (GWAMFANCI, GWAMFI, ABAANGI, BANGA, BANGANCI, BANGAWA), WURI (WURANCI, WURAWA). 'Bangawa' is the Hausa name for the people, 'Banganci' for the language; 'Lyase' means 'mother tongue'. The two dialects have slight lexical and tonal differences. Many Gwamfawa are assimilating to Lela culture and language while the Wurawa are assimilating to Hausa. The Gwamfawa are around Danko and the Wurawa around Maga.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Secondhand database remark that the Gwamhi and Wuri dialects differ (slightly) in tone, which presupposes lexical/grammatical tone in the language; no tone inventory, no word-stress remark.
new_statements.identity_note: Entry is explicitly GWAMHI-WURI [BGA], 8,000 (1973 SIL), Sokoto (now Kebbi) State, Gwamfawa around Danko and Wurawa around Maga = exactly gwam1244; dialects GWAMHI (GWAMFANCI, GWAMFI, ABAANGI, BANGA, BANGANCI, BANGAWA), WURI (WURANCI, WURAWA). Glottolog lists Ethnologue 16th ed. for gwam1244; our bibliography lists no Ethnologue edition.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. [2011]. The Northwest Kainji languages (web page, rogerblench.info/., the Internet Archive 2015) + full the Internet Archive's index listing of the Kainji directory tree
sources.note: Group-level note only (Northwest Kainji defined by consonantal noun prefixes). Only was ever posted under Northwest/; no Gwamhi or Wuri wordlist/phonology file appears in 592 archived URLs.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 1), 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1314323.
sources.note: No phonology for this language: the chapter's only Gwamhi content is its place in the Northwest Kainji tree and the typological note 'Reduced affix system with C- prefixes and concord'. General remarks on tone concern the author's transcription practice ('Tone-marking in particular is somewhat impressionistic'; mid tone unmarked in three-tone languages such as Reshe) and other branches (Reshe prefix tones, East Kainji), never Wurə-Gwamhyə-Mba. Nothing on stress anywhere in sec.3.3.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012. 369 pp. (Internet Archive copy of rogerblench.info)
sources.note: sec.3.8.4 'Wəri-Gwamhyə-Mba' (pp.29-30) is sociolinguistic (autonyms, villages, vitality, wordlists taken 2010-11); the only prosodic remark is p.30 'The differences [between the three lects] are said to largely lie in the tonation.' sec.4.8.4 'Wuri cluster' under 4. Phonology (p.36) is an empty heading. Comparative wordlist appendix gives untoned Gwamhyə/Wurə/Gwamhɪ-R forms. No stress statement.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. In S. McGill & P. K. Austin (eds), Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135. London: SOAS.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.121: 'Wuri and Gwamhy are two ethnic groups speaking dialects of a single language, completely undescribed apart from a few nouns in Rowlands (1962).' Sociolinguistic vitality report only (fieldwork 2011-12 at Bori near Maga).

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2012. The Kainji languages. Unpublished report prepared for the Niger-Congo workshop (file 'kainji_report_2012-08-30'), 7 pp. Posted on the LLACAN 'Niger-Congo' pages (llacan.vjf.cnrs.fr/fichiers/nigercongo/fichiers/). = Glottolog ref 306337.
sources.note: Sec. 1.3 'Linguistic features' is family-level only: vowel systems (6- or 8-vowel with ɘ), vowel-harmony types, implosives/labiovelars, syllable structure ('Northwest languages such as C'Lela where complex clusters are common'), and one tonal remark about another branch ('in Sengwe they are more often monosyllabic with a correspondingly more complex tonal inventory'). Nothing is said about tone or stress in Gwamhi-Wuri specifically; the language appears only in the wordlist inventory with tone-marked autonyms [ɘ̀dwɘ́ɾì] (Wuri) and [ɘ̀dɡʷàmhʲɘ́ˀ] (Gwamhi) - wordlist-level tone marks, not a sta…
